findings.what: "One wound with its coils pressed tight needs a pull before it stretches at all, so its line misses zero" has no source in the lesson's list or in research-notes.md (no quote on initial tension or close-coiled springs), so either cite one or cut the clause; the Bitesize quote only backs the through-origin case.

findings.where: screen 12 (Read its law), the two points on line C
findings.what: The two points read off the line sit at the same loads as the first and last readings (line 12 N vs reading 12.4 N, line 42 N vs reading 41.7 N, about 2 px apart on the 0-60 N axis), so the '12 N' label looks like it names the first reading. That is the slip the P = 0.15W + 12.4 option and its hint warn against, and it blurs the lesson's rule 'from the line, never from the readings'. Read the line between readings instead, for example 15 N at 60 N and 39 N at 220 N: rise 24 ÷ run 160 = 0.15, b = 15 − 0.15 × 60 = 6 (checked by hand). Screen 10 has the same overlap at 12 mm (line 30 N on the 29.9 N reading), though it does less harm there.

The longest-stick label '1.2 Ω' sits just under the 30 °C reading, whose stick is 0.8 Ω, rather than beside the 20 °C stick it measures (11.8 − 10.6 = 1.2), so at 360 px it reads as the wrong stick's length; place it against the 20 °C stick.

The graph changes from a 9.5-14.5 Ω scale to a 0-24 Ω scale without a word, so readings that rose steeply on screens 1-4 suddenly look nearly flat; add a few words such as 'zoomed out to show 0 Ω' to screen 5's text.

findings.where: screen 11 (Which line fits?), line C picked
findings.what: On the 0-60 N axis, line C's sticks are 0.3-0.5 N (about 2 px), so 'spread along it' can only be read from the count and not seen; consider labelling C's longest stick or saying 'sticks too short to see' in the Why.

"How strongly many materials resist current changes with temperature in approximately a straight line" is a garden-path sentence (the verb 'changes' comes late); try "In many materials, resistance changes with temperature along roughly a straight line."

findings.where: explain, last paragraph; closing line after screen 12
findings.what: "Textbooks add that a method called least squares calculates the line instead" has no footnote and does not say where it is taught, though the brief promised 'least squares comes at college' (HN Analytical Methods, Modern Engineering Mathematics 2.3.2, notes 4.7). Cite it and say it comes at college, ideally also on the last screen beside the Exponentials and logarithms pointer.

findings.where: lesson as a whole versus brief section 2, lesson 6

The rule line 'Law: P = aW + b, with a the gradient and b the intercept' sits directly above the ask row 'Law: P = ?', so 'Law:' appears twice in a row; relabel the ask row, for example 'Line C: P = ?'.

The lesson column and its 22rem graph sit flush left in the wide card, leaving the right 60% of the laptop view empty, and the graph is no bigger than on a phone; centre the column if the house layout allows.
